rationale: The exact corrected decision properly leaves whole-order status unresolved; its rationale now accurately distinguishes partial/conditional displacement from complete revocation. EO 13881 §§1–5, 84 FR 34257–34259 (PDF pp.1–3). Section 2 requires consideration of FAR amendments, public-comment evaluation, a final rule if appropriate and agency conformity regulations; §3 contains immediate inconsistency supersession plus a conditional revocation of two EO 10582 subsections; §4 requires a report on further FAR changes. One-time tasks, conditional amendment effects and potential continuing implementation must be distinguished. EO 14005 §14(b), 86 FR 7478 (PDF p.4), supersedes EO 13881 only to the extent inconsistent. EO 14005 §8 directs consideration of new content tests and increased preferences, which does not on its face extinguish every command or executed legal effect of EO 13881. Its §14(a) outright revocations do not include EO 13881. EO 13881 §5 preserves statutory authority, including nonavailability/public-interest exceptions. Sections 2–4 may be completed, displaced or still relevant in different ways, but the necessary rule issuance, actual performance and current provision comparison are not supplied. Effects of §3 on EO 10582 require their own accounting rather than automatic restoration or extinction. EO 14148's complete revocation list omits EO 14005 and EO 13881. It provides no whole-order answer for this conditional-supersession case.
